hyps.why: At already-large learning rates Adam diverges or becomes unstable, so increasing further hurts much more than elsewhere.
At tiny learning rates the network is undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing the step size gives large gains.
Stepping back from an unstable learning rate recovers a lot of accuracy.
Small batches already give many noisy updates, so raising the learning rate pushes training into instability sooner.
With a tiny learning rate, fewer updates per epoch from larger batches worsen undertraining.
More updates per epoch compensate for a small step size.
Near alpha=1 the L2 penalty causes underfitting, so further increases hurt substantially while at small alpha they are negligible.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening them helps more than widening already-wide networks.
Deeper ReLU networks are less stable at large learning rates, so adding depth increases divergence risk.
A shallower network is more stable at large step sizes, so removing a layer helps more there.
